Luke never signs his Gospel. So who wrote it, when, and who was "Theophilus" meant to convince?
Halfway through Acts, the narrator suddenly says "we". Was the author really on board?
Why does Luke's Gospel begin, and end, in the Temple, with shepherds and old prophets as witnesses?

an-introduction-to-the-acts-of-the-apost: Jesus leaves, and ten days later a small praying group starts preaching to crowds. What changed?

Weeks after denying Jesus, Peter faces the court that condemned him. Why does he not back down?
Did the first Christians all preach the same message, and are these Peter's own words?
Seven men were chosen to hand out food. Why did two of them end up changing where the faith went?

When Christians share bread and wine, what do they believe they are really receiving?
an-introduction-to-islam: What was Makkah like before Islam, and how did an orphan become its most trusted man?

How did a man who fled Makkah by night return eight years later as its leader?

Can it be right to break a moral rule without doing anything morally evil?

afterlife-body-soul: If everything you see is changing, how could anyone know what is truly real?

religious-experience: A blinding light, a silent sense of presence, a terror before the holy: are these the same experience?
